Consult Summary:
- Young adult with 2 days of progressive, constant lower abdominal (suprapubic) burning pain with subjective feverishness, mild nausea, increased urinary frequency and pink-appearing urine; empiric oral antibiotics (trimethoprim) prescribed and pregnancy test/urine testing recommended.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Lower abdominal (just below the umbilicus) pain for ~2 days, described as burning, constant, progressively worse, tender to pressure.
  - Subjective feeling hot and sweaty.
  - Mild nausea; no vomiting.
  - Pink-appearing urine noted; uncertain if true hematuria.
  - Increased urinary frequency; no dysuria reported.
  - Recent constipation last week that has since improved; current bowel movements normal.
- Timeline:
  - Symptoms began approximately 2 days ago and have been gradually worsening.
  - Last sexual activity ~4 days ago.
  - Last STD screen normal ~6 months ago.
  - Implanon inserted ~1 year ago.
  - Last menstrual period: patient first said ~3 weeks ago then corrected to ~2 weeks ago (conflict noted).
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Pain worsened by pressure on abdomen (tender to palpation reported by patient).
  - Drinking increased fluids; patient attributing increased urinary frequency in part to fluid intake.
  - Paracetamol advised for analgesia.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - No vomiting.
  - No measured fever (subjective hot/sweaty only).
  - No cough, dyspnea, palpitations, headaches, or visual changes.
  - No vaginal bleeding reported.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No dysuria or burning with urination.
  - No diarrhea or ongoing constipation at time of consult.
  - No prior similar episodes.

Past Medical History:
- No known chronic medical conditions reported.
- No prior surgeries.
- Implanon contraceptive implant in situ for ~1 year.

Medications:
- Implanon (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Trimethoprim prescribed during visit:
  - Instruction documented in transcript as "one tablet twice a day for three days."
  - Conflict noted: physician also said "take two tablets" earlier in the same instruction (conflict noted regarding number of tablets to take).
Allergies:
- Not stated in transcript.

Social History:
- Lives in a share house with two roommates.
- Employed as an accountant.
- Non-smoker.
- Drinks alcohol socially; no excessive use reported.
- Sexually active with a single partner; no barrier contraception used in addition to Implanon.

Family History:
- No relevant family history reported or known.

Physical Examination:
- No vital signs documented.
- No physical examination findings documented (patient reported abdominal tenderness to self-palpation; no clinician exam findings recorded).

Investigations:
- No investigations/results available in the transcript.
- Physician stated tests would be useful and could be organized today (unspecified). Physician specifically recommended a pregnancy test and urine testing to help determine cause.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected urinary tract infection vs other causes of lower abdominal pain
  - Assessment: Lower abdominal burning pain with increased urinary frequency and pink urine — UTI is a possible diagnosis among other differentials (gut-related pain, pregnancy-related causes as discussed).
  - Plan:
    - Empiric oral antibiotic prescribed: Trimethoprim — documented instruction: "one tablet twice a day for three days." Conflict noted with earlier statement "take two tablets."
    - Advise increased oral fluids.
    - Recommend cranberry juice for urinary symptom support.
    - Arrange urine testing to help confirm/exclude UTI (physician stated tests could be organized today).
- Issue 2: Possible pregnancy
  - Assessment: Pregnancy considered given contraceptive implant may fail rarely; last period timing uncertain.
  - Plan:
    - Recommend pregnancy test to be performed (physician advised patient to take a pregnancy test and clinician to consider it).
- Issue 3: Symptom control and safety-netting
  - Assessment: Ongoing abdominal pain with subjective feverishness and nausea.
  - Plan:
    - Paracetamol for pain/fever as needed.
    - Safety-netting: Return or call if symptoms worsen or do not improve in a few days; specifically watch for worsening abdominal pain, persistent high temperature, persistent vomiting.
    - Patient advised to collect antibiotic prescription from pharmacy (physician sent script to pharmacy).
    - Follow-up arranged as needed if no improvement.

General Plan items:
- Clinician offered to organize tests today to clarify diagnosis.
- Patient instructed to start antibiotics as prescribed and to perform pregnancy testing.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Allergies not documented in transcript.
  - Complete medication reconciliation not documented (only Implanon and new antibiotic mentioned).
  - Vital signs and clinician physical examination findings not recorded.
  - Results of any investigations (urine test, pregnancy test) not available.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Trimethoprim dosing instruction inconsistent: physician said both "take two tablets" and "one tablet twice a day for three days" (conflict noted).
  - Timing of last menstrual period: patient first said "about three weeks ago" then corrected to "two weeks ago" (conflict noted).
  - Patient name referenced as "Tim" by clinician early in transcript and later addressed as "Kim" (conflict/noted possible transcript name confusion).
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally audible and intelligible with some filler words and brief hesitations; clinical content clear.
